changelog:
ETF Preserve v9.0 — MAJOR: the same rules-based, point-in-time fund pool and true-volatility budget as ETF Growth v9.0, under Preserve's posture.

1. Rules-based, point-in-time pool shared with Growth: 22 dated pools ("Rule pool v5 (C12) — as-of 2004…2025") through dynamic_menu.pool_schedule; declaration data/exposures/arms/dt-C12.json; pool constitution v5 + R19 + R20.
2. Fund rules R19 (levered market: beta ≥ 1.3 AND sector drift ≥ 0.15 — today SPHB) and R20 (12-month holdings stability ≥ 0.453 — today removes MTUM, SPMO, XMMO, XSMO), re-measured each January.
3. Declared broad seats exempt from the tail screen; gold rated on its own scale and sized by equal risk.
4. Strength cap 0.40 in the harvest objective; true book volatility ≤ 1.8 × SPY (cutting planes); world active-risk row ≤ 1.05 × SPY (75th percentile by rule; world = VTI 0.564 / EFA 0.353 / EEM 0.083).
5. Rebound-boost refutation needs two consecutive closes below the 40-day average.
6. Preserve's posture is unchanged (floor 0.40, rebound posture solve, cash when the defensive sleeve is empty).

Measured (first-of-month path, 2006 → 2026-10-23, vs v8.1.2): CAGR 14.83% vs 14.05%, Martin 4.556 vs 3.944. Panel: centre 14.13% vs 13.33% (+0.80pp); stress gate passes on all four arms; off-path Martin +0.27, worst-12mo −0.04pp, worst-3m +0.19pp; absolute floors every arm (maxDD worst −15.6% vs −22%, worst-12mo worst −10.4% vs −15%); cadence panel passes every band including worst-3m. Years behind SPY 5 (v8: 3). Walk §8.422–§8.428.

D6 acknowledged: Devon 2026-10-29: cohorts behind regresses +0.99pp off-path (+0.65pp first-of-month). It is the end-dated share of start dates still behind SPY at 2026-10-23, dominated by 2026 starts — v8's 2026 semiconductor run (16.7% vs 12.8%). Every other D6 measure improves off-path: RDD3y −0.90pp, longest underwater −883 days, long-bull trailing windows −7.87pp.

Disclosures: as ETF Growth v9.0 — rules developed against 2006–2025 (in-sample), 2026 holdings definitions, survivors only, bond sleeve unchanged.

[major: Two new methodologies: the offensive fund pool is built by mechanical rules point-in-time (22 dated pools rebuilt each January, data-driven fund rules) instead of a hand-curated list; and the allocation's volatility budget constrains the book's TRUE volatility (and its active risk vs a world index) by an exact cutting-plane solve instead of a sum of own volatilities.
